6.status_line: Closed — five versions tagged; every cut minor now carries a done-definition
6.goal: No goal was stated at the start — the sprint rhythm had lapsed, and direction came from a live steer rather than a written goal. Ben, opening: "cut as many versions as we can now, rather than working on the lofty, conceptual stuff."

retro.landed: Five versions tagged — v0.1.1 (the word interface), v0.1.2 (buildings rework), v0.1.8 (build health), v0.1.9 (shell & legibility), v0.1.10 (generation & content) — against zero in the preceding six days. 24 backlog items closed; open items 97 → 77 despite 13 new items filed. Every cut minor now carries a done-definition, written at its cut — that was the structural fix, not the tags. The gate went from lying to green: had been reporting ten failures of which exactly one was a failing assertion; v0.1.8 re-tiered it, and v0.1.10 closed with 55 tests, 0 failures — the first fully green gate of the arc. Four stub minors stopped being design-only: BL-342-345 turn v0.1.3/v0.1.4/v0.1.6 into buildable work, on the finding that BL-155 and BL-156 had both settled on the same condition_set object and neither built it.
retro.feedback: Held: worktree sub-agents did the bulk of the work and several outperformed their briefs — one refused its own instructions because BL-216 §1-3 was superseded by a complete item and implementing it would have reverted a landed decision; another volunteered that a knife-edge test had influenced its parameter choice (BL-349). Did not hold: three of five agents in the v0.1.9 batch branched from a base that had already moved, and every one produced code that would not merge cleanly — worktrees isolate writes, not history. The v0.1.10 batch was worse: one agent's commit swallowed a whole fast-forward (328 files) and cost 36 conflicts to integrate. Integration read every hunk rather than trusting a clean auto-merge, and that is why the Ages view and the disclosure controls survived.

6.notes: Diagnosis before any work: 119 commits since the v0.1.0 tag and not one version cut, with CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] still reading "Nothing yet" — the changelog was not merely un-stamped, it was not accruing. Root cause (NR-103): the roadmap wrote done-definitions for exactly two versions, v0.1.0 and v1.0.0 — and those were the only two ever cut or scheduled. A theme with no done-definition has no test for finished, so it absorbs items indefinitely (v0.1.1 was the proof: its three theme legs shipped 2026-08-03, and 26 unrelated items were then retrofitted onto the same tag over the following week). Measurement overturned the stated cause four times: BL-338 wetland (story: relief commits displaced it; measured: refuted by rebuilding the audit at 802421c^ — identical census, wetland is a drainage feature and elevation had no vote in composition), BL-347 econ tick (story: an O(n log n) sort; measured: the sort was 3%, cost was std::map allocation in worlds with no stacks), BL-346 estimator (story: BL-079's reflex reads an inflated number; measured: retracted — that function reads realised credit, real site was the pre-build estimator), pan "lag" (story: needs a 200ms input delay; measured: panning costs nothing, static and panning measured identically — it was 157k vertices at whole-grid zoom). A green gate can lie: logistics_reach_harness failed three assertions from byte-identical sources — a conflict-heavy merge left ninja holding a stale object that touch would not dislodge. Standing lesson: --clean-first before cutting after a messy merge, and if a harness fails suspiciously, build the same commit in a throwaway worktree before believing it. Left for another session: v0.1.11 open with four items (generation globe BL-256, deed history lines BL-309, BL-348 province names half-native, BL-349); v0.1.3-v0.1.7 remain uncut and are next in sequence; 42 items still sit at post-v0.1.0 (NR-101's finding); Windows work owed (stale visual/MSVC goldens, BL-341 parked).

retro.feedback: Twice, the expensive-looking job turned out to be a bookkeeping job, at different scales: (1) BL-342 is about thirty lines of switch statement, and it unblocked two minors that had been design-forward for weeks — BL-155 and BL-156 had independently settled on the same object (a flat AND-list of atomic conditions) and neither built it, because each was scoped design-only; the blocker was ownership, not effort, nobody owned the thing they both needed. (2) NR-101 was the same finding at document level: twenty of the 45 unversioned items were already assigned by ROADMAP.md in prose (the whole v0.4.0 politics substrate, most of the v0.3.0 Era −1 arc) — the roadmap and the backlog disagreed, and the disagreement was invisible because the prose was not queryable and the query did not read prose. Sprint 6's lesson was measure before you fix; Sprint 7's is adjacent: before estimating a blocked thing, check whether anything is actually blocking it. The design test earned its keep concretely: BL-094 asks "does this system reach military as well as economic outcomes?" — it changed two decisions this sprint at no extra cost (condition_set shipped military_units/military_strength alongside six economic subjects; the tech gate went on the Military Base rather than a smelter). Two collisions between the sprint's own decisions, both caught by writing the assertion first: BL-342 established that an empty condition_set is true (common case for a law); BL-344 then needed the opposite for a tech (~130 authored nodes with no gate would have earned themselves on the first tick) — fixed with a separate earnable flag: absence has to be modelled by absence, not by an empty predicate. Second collision was structural: the predicate could not live in tech_tree.cpp, because that TU pulls in sol2 and is excluded from the world superset a harness links.

7.notes: Where the method held: by not doing the thing — Sprint 6's worst cost was worktree agents branching from a moved base (36 conflicts to integrate one commit); this sprint's three items were one dependency chain across ~2 files each, so built sequentially in the main session, stated as a call rather than defaulted into. The bench prediction paid off exactly: econ_stability and home_surface_bench failed at -j 4 and passed re-run idle, precisely as the v0.1.9 retro said they would (they assert absolute wall-clock, so they measure the machine). Where it did not hold: the JSON stores got corrupted three times — long resolution prose full of backticks (condition_set, apply_budget, earnable) inside a shell heredoc are command substitution, the shell silently deletes the word and mangled text lands in the canonical store looking almost right; three repair passes; fixed durably by writing edit scripts to a file and running them, saved to memory. The pacing signal is not being collected — third consecutive entry whose Runtime line reads "not tracked": tools/session/timer.js exists, the format block asks for the number explicitly, and nobody starts it; the commit span measures the landing, not the work. Left for another session: NR-115 (world generation places starting military bases through the tile-only check, so a corp can begin a campaign with a base it has not researched — defensible as fiction, a one-line fix either way); NR-102 (sequencing decoupling, now the standing structural item — a minor per item is not an order to build them in); v0.1.5/6/7 remain uncut, v0.1.11 now carries ten items (largest open minor); Windows work still owed.

10.notes: Why v0.1.13 rather than a new minor: hollowed out 2026-08-10 when BL-340 left for v0.1.14, leaving five items with no A-priority — this gives it a keystone and rescues two C-items into a coherent story. Why this precedes procurement: BL-350's counterparty model needs suppliers to choose between; against today's 8 lean corps and ~24 buildings on 15,120 tiles, "another supplier may still quote" is often simply false and the mechanic would ship correct but unexercised (exactly Sprint 9's hire_unit: shipped correct, never once observed firing across five harness seeds, NR-121). Ordering this first also DELETES BL-340's substrate step rather than building it twice, since BL-365 removes the function that step would have extended. The measurement that motivated it: pregame_balance_harness 80 (2026-08-10, real generated world) — player corp balance grows linearly to tick 23, knees at ~24, plateaus from ~tick 47 at ~185k cr; the economy has a carrying capacity and reaches it. 26.goal: ENSURE SPECTATOR MODE WORKS, AND VISIBLY WATCH AI PLAY IN ORDER TO FURTHER DEVELOP THE META (Ben, 2026-08-31). That is the sprint in one sentence and everything else is subordinate to it. Spectate is today reachable only from a --verify script, and the decision feed reads ‘overridden’ at 0.00 on every row, so the two things needed to WATCH are both absent or broken - they are the sprint. Behind them sits the design the watching is meant to inform: restraint lives in the world, not the agent (AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from), so no corp holds itself back and instead LEADING IS EXPENSIVE - coalitions form against whoever leads. The close race becomes an emergent property rather than a target any actor aims at. What is learned by watching feeds docs/ai/STRATEGIES.md, which owns the meta.
planned: BL-695 (live spectate route) - FIRST. Spectate is reachable ONLY from a --verify script today (verify.spectate is the single assignment site in the tree), so "watch the AI play in real time" is not currently possible from the running game. Everything else is watched through this.

BL-696 (decision feed reasons) - FIRST, with it. NR-626: every feed row reads ‘overridden’ at 0.00, so the only window onto rival reasoning is blank. And a coalition that cannot be READ is just a hidden handicap again, which is the exact thing the reframe rejects.

BL-699 (rival coalitions) - THE BRAKE, and the sprint’s real deliverable. The four stance verbs from BL-448 exist and the scorer issues none of them. Stance scores against standing, so the leader accumulates enemies and the field accumulates friends.

BL-701 (climate doc) - DONE 2026-08-31, documentation only per Ben. Rewritten twice more the same day: climate runs on planetology's scalars unfrozen (NOT tile hazard), and it is the NEXT Era's catastrophe, outside prototype scope. The Era catastrophe model itself was promoted out of the research doc into ERAS.md § The point of an Era in the same pass (NR-750).

BL-702 (spectate god view control) - with BL-695. god_view is read at every site and written only by verify.god_view. Spectating without it is watching silhouettes.

BL-705 (selectable 1960s start) - Ben, 2026-08-31: "we will be working on the 1960s start". The branch is live and unreachable; nothing in src/ ever sets epoch_year. Also fixes the hard-coded 1960 epoch constant, which a 1960s start would otherwise make accidentally correct.

26.notes:
THE REFRAME, and it is the whole sprint. Ben, 2026-08-31: "The angle we are taking here is a literal handicap. I prefer to consider it as always a force from within the game system. With 7 corporations, we have plenty of room for alliances to form against leaders, and we haven't built a critical system which is climate." He named the contradiction with his own earlier steer himself and chose to keep both modes, with the systemic one as the foundation. NR-746 records the supersession; NR-743 (margin measured against the strongest corp) is answered by it and should be read as historical.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT ON EVERY BRAKE, Ben the same day: "'how far restraint goes' should never exclude extension and construction. If a player loses out, they should be able to see that the world doesn't wait for them." A pressured corp still builds. A brake scales what a corp does and never forbids a category of it. This binds BL-698 and BL-699 equally and is written into AI_OPPONENT.md § The constraint on restraint.

ORDERING: instruments (BL-695, BL-696, BL-700, BL-697) before the brake (BL-699). Three of those exist because the thing that would have shown or measured the brake is broken or absent.

SCOPE HONESTY: climate is a system, not an item, and is deliberately design-only here. If the sprint runs long, BL-699 is the item to protect - it can produce a close race on its own, and climate is what later makes that race fair when the PLAYER is the one leading.

STILL UNOWNED after this sprint (NR-744): lobbying, nation stance gating the player, and the Stage C dialogue layer - purged as BL-539/BL-540/BL-334 while their dated grants still stand in the standing rules.

BEN'S RESTATED AIM, 2026-08-31, and it narrows the sprint rather than adding to it: "Our aim for sprint 26 is to ensure spectator mode works, and visibly watch AI play in order to further develop the meta." Read BL-695 and BL-696 as the sprint's actual deliverable and BL-699 as what makes watching worth doing. If the sprint runs short, a working spectate route plus a feed that reads is a GOOD outcome on its own - the coalitions can slip. The reverse is not true: coalitions landed but unwatchable would leave the sprint unable to say whether they work.

THE META IS A DOCUMENT AND IT SHOULD RECEIVE THE OUTPUT. docs/ai/STRATEGIES.md owns the meta, authored ahead of the game as research rather than authority. Watching real rival play is the first chance to check that authored meta against what the scorer actually does; expect edits to it, and treat a divergence as a finding about one or the other rather than a defect in the scorer by default.

CLIMATE LEFT THE SPRINT AND LEFT THE PROTOTYPE, 2026-08-31. Ben: "I am not against climate change being a large problem for Era 2, but our prototype works solely on Era 1 for now." CLIMATE.md is rewritten as the NEXT Era's catastrophe and is out of scope. ONE KNOCK-ON MATTERS HERE: AI_OPPONENT.md had named climate as the second systemic brake on a runaway leader, so COALITIONS NOW CARRY THAT BRAKE ALONE. If BL-699 does not brake a runaway in this sprint, nothing else will - and that is a finding about coalitions, not a reason to reach for BL-698's opt-in dial.

THE LADDER IS 1-BASED AND THE START IS THE 1960s (Ben, 2026-08-31, resolving NR-749). Era 1 Terrestrial, catastrophe nuclear war - that is the era this sprint watches. Era 2 Early Space, catastrophe climate. The renumber is the DOCUMENT's Era axis only; era_band, condition_subject::era and every E0-/E1- tech id are untouched and nothing in src/ moved. One divergence created and tracked: the F9 mock viewer still labels its tabs by the old numbers (NR-751), and ACTIONS.md correctly still mirrors the viewer rather than the docs.
26.retro:
GOAL MET, AND AT WAVE 1. Ben's sentence was "ensure spectator mode works, and visibly watch AI play in order to further develop the meta". The first half landed whole: --spectate opens a session with nobody seated, the god-view control was already there, the decision feed reports real scores and reasons, a composite standing index exists, and the 1960s start is selectable. The second half produced a finding rather than a meta, and the finding is worth more than the meta would have been.

THE FINDING. Every AI corp goes bankrupt on every seed - net worth -624k to -1.2M, insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30, final == min so it never recovers. Measured with ai_skill_harness, confirmed from both ends (the slice agent stashed its own change and got the same digits; an independent baseline without the slice reproduced it).

THE CAUSE, measured with demand_census on the industrial band: iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000. Five of the eight designed demand channels do not exist, and of the three that do, Industry ships its rates at zero. The AI is not playing badly - it is playing a game with no demand side, and no scorer improvement can move that.

SO WAVE 2 WAS CANCELLED RATHER THAN BUILT. BL-699's coalitions form against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is the least bankrupt; its weights are the whole design and would need redoing the moment demand lands. Cancelling was cheaper than tuning against noise. Ben's call, 2026-08-31: "Close sprint 26 at wave 1 and unpause demand."

WHAT THE SPRINT ACTUALLY SPENT ITS TIME ON, and this is the retro's real lesson: FOUR BUILD-WIRING BREAKS, none caused by this sprint, none caught by any test. main had not configured for eight commits; the whole verifier-headless tier could not compile; build_app.bat failed in any worktree; demand_census had never linked. Two of the four were MASKED BY STALE PREBUILT BINARIES THAT PASS. The sprint fixed all four before reaching its own work. NR-759 owns the pattern.

ONE ITEM CLOSED UNBUILT. BL-702's premise was wrong - the god-view control had existed since BL-408. It was filed on a grep for `god_view =`, which cannot find a write through a pointer. The agent found it by reading the file rather than trusting the brief.

ONE ITEM DELIVERED MORE THAN ASKED. BL-705 was briefed to make the epoch dynamic; it found that campaign_epoch_year was one name over two quantities - a serialised history datum and a live display value - welded by a static_assert, which is what pinned the calendar at 1960 while campaigns generated at 0 CE. The check was retired rather than replaced.

WORKTREES: three agents, three slices, one real merge conflict (two slices adding CLI flags at the same site), all absorbed. Every agent was briefed to verify its own base and every one of them found the base wrong - worktrees are cut from a diverged origin/main (NR-753). The discipline worked; the instruction wording needs a branch for 'sideways' as well as 'behind'.

31.theme: Long-term market viability - every recipe pays at base price
31.status_line: CLOSED 2026-09-02 on Ben's call, stage one a SUCCESS: the field ends the standard thirty-year lapse with a majority of corps operating-positive (46 of 61, 31 of 55) where it began with four and none, debtors a tenth of the field, median balances climbing, buildings running. 31.goal: A robust market in which every player - human or rival - can make a steady profit. Ben, 2026-09-02: "the simplest way to do this is to ensure that all recipes (at base price) make a greater profit than marginal costs" - the obvious part the demand work walked past. Stated as two halves (PRODUCTION.md § The recipe margin anchor): M1, at base price every recipe's margin is at least k x its marginal cost (inputs at base + wage per batch), k authored at 1.0 = profit at least equal to marginal cost; M2, at the price FLOOR a building at typical staffing still covers maintenance, goods upkeep and wages (BL-740's form, for the whole roster). Both are checked at AUTHORING TIME against the three tables, never against live prices, so every other lever - demand composition, the band, the scorer - sits on a roster that can pay. Then MEASURE the field again: the anchor is necessary, not sufficient; the 2026-09-01 ledger's structural -755/qtr and the year-30 debt spiral (interest 96% of net loss) are separate levers and stay named.
planned: BL-744 (recipe margin anchor) - FIRST. The instrument half is built: tools/verify/recipe_margin prices every processing recipe and every extraction target in both bands, prints the table, asserts the two halves with a differential red-proof. The retune half is the sprint's real work: turn R1-R4 green without simply lifting every output price. Order of preference, from NR-776: (1) processing base_rate and the wage/maintenance side - wage 12 over 8 batches is 1.50 per batch and is often the WHOLE margin, maintenance 10/tick against 4 batches at W=0.5 wants 2.50 per batch at base and 10 per batch at the floor; (2) input quantities where a recipe is authored at zero or negative value-add (steel_from_blooms 22 in for 8 out, consumer_goods 14 in for 12 out, hydroponics_bay 6.25 in for 3 out); (3) base prices last, up the chain in order, with ceil_mult re-derived after.

campaign_lapse (BL-723) on the industrial 1960 band is the done-when instrument: mean operating net, operating-positive corps, valued production, debtor count - the same four the sweeps already log.
31.risk: Anchoring by raising output prices alone compounds up the chain: every tier's inputs rise with the tier below, the ladder widens past the 56x the space premise rests on, and ceil_mult re-derives upward. Retune from rates and costs first, prices last. Two bands share one price table, so a retune that fixes one can break the other - the harness runs both and both must clear. And the anchor is necessary, not sufficient: a roster that pays at base still loses collectively if the money entering the field is less than what leaves, so the lapse measurement stays the verdict and the anchor is the precondition for it meaning anything.

THE PLAYER WATCHES THE WORLD BE MADE, and generation hands the campaign a world whose trade and grudges have a cause.

ROUND 4 IS PASS 1, THE POLITY PASS. A 2D map replaces the globe and runs a time-lapse of 4000 years to 1200 CE, with an ordered scoreboard of the top sixteen on the left. WHAT IT SET OUT TO DO, AND WHAT IT DELIVERED. Ben asked for three specific trees, a view on their size, on arranging nodes without jumps, on what a polity with research to spare wants, and then the Empire scorer. All four are written: TREES.md carries the grammar and the five lintable rules, the three docs carry 143 nodes between them, and every Empire node carries the situation in which it is pursued. The build is deliberately NOT this sprint's - Ben closed it here rather than build trees onto phases that have not landed.

WHAT WORKED. Writing the LINT before the content. Both sub-agents were briefed against a rule set that already ran, so their first clean lint was a real bar and not a self-report; the Colonisation agent found the grammar could not express "any two of four" and said so instead of bending the store to pass. Two grammar additions came out of that, both lintable, both recorded to be overturned (NR-820).

WHAT THE DOCS DID NOT KNOW. COLONISATION.md names no farm class; the classifier names twelve. The brief assumed four and the tree was sized for four, and it was the agent reading the CODE that found it - the doc is silent where the code is authority, and a brief written from the doc alone inherits the silence (NR-819). The same shape as the standing "backlog prose goes stale" lesson, one layer up.

WHAT MOVED UNDER THE STATED NUMBERS. The assessment said 2 / 3 / 4 milestones; the spire rule gives one per ring, so 3 / 4 / 4 (NR-822). And the "two or three minors per major" reference ratio does not survive a 64-node cap - the trees run near one minor per two majors, and TREES.md now says a minor exists where a jump needs bridging, with no ratio to hit. Both were caught by writing the thing rather than describing it.

SMALL TOOLING FRICTION, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT PAID TWICE. A Python heredoc on Windows reads stdin as cp1252 and fails to match any line with a section sign; PYTHONUTF8=1 or a script file. A bash heredoc holding a long JS literal tripped the tool's quoting; a script file in the scratchpad did not.

WHAT IS OWED. The build, in the pool: BL-881 (empire tree in sim) first, and its first decision is how a JSON store reaches a Lua-free sim. The farm-class fold (NR-819) before BL-882. Every magnitude is a placeholder until BL-886.

CLOSED 2026-08-21 having overshot its own done_when by five items. The goal — provinces grown from settlement and stopped by terrain — was met by BL-515 before this session opened. WHAT THE SPRINT ACTUALLY PROVED, and it is a method claim rather than a feature one:

1. THE METHOD NOTE HELD A SECOND TIME. The sprint's own note says every ruling that stuck was made against a RENDER, not a spec. BL-519 repeated it in a form nobody had budgeted for: the forest-on-rock threshold was set at the value the design implied (moisture >= 0.55), MEASURED, and found to fire zero times — because the biome table only ever draws rocky ground in the dry and middling columns, so wet rock does not exist for the branch to find. 2. A REFACTOR CAN BE MADE FALSIFIABLE, and it is worth the structure. BL-519 was 522 references across ~110 files. 3. THE CEILING RULING GENERALISED IMMEDIATELY. NR-438's shape — a stated number becomes a PREFERENCE, a real bound is ASSERTED, and the over-share is REPORTED because 'rare' was never defined — was reused within hours by BL-516's sea provinces, which hit exactly the same wall at 82 against 'say 80' (NR-460). A ruling that produces a reusable discipline is worth more than one that produces a number.

4. THE FAN-OUT COST AN HOUR, and the cause is filed (NR-459). Three agents ran concurrently; all three got worktrees at the SESSION's base rather than at HEAD. One fast-forwarded itself, one did not and built an entire item against the enum BL-519 had just deleted. The port was cheap only because that agent had routed every water test through one choke-point predicate. Two agents also independently minted the same review ids, because NEEDS_REVIEW.json has no next_id.js. Both are process fixes, not judgement failures.

WHAT IS OWED, and it is the honest weakness of the whole arc: NOTHING WAS RENDERED. Four of the six items have a UI half, and the session ran in a container that cannot build the GUI. Everything is compile-clean against real ImGui headers and arithmetically checked; none of it has been seen. No golden was blessed, because blessing an unseen frame pins whatever got built. For a sprint whose own method note is 'build it, look at it, then rule', ending without the looking is the thing to fix — and BL-521, built this same session, is what makes the looking cheap next time.

CARRIED FORWARD: BL-518 (the Era -1 sim redrawing borders as its wars resolve) is the last clause of Ben's brief and is still design-owed with three undecided questions. BL-514 (blend all tiles) stays HELD, and BL-520 has now given it a second reason to be decided — texture and the blend are in direct tension.

32a.risk: THE ABSTRACTION. Two engines (the polity sim with regions and rounds; the economy tick with firms and credits) and one handoff between them - if pass 3 reads pass 2's internals the two engines fuse and neither stays cheap. Keep the handoff a struct of plain outputs. THE PRECONDITION. THE COST. Pass 1 is already the most expensive pass; pass 2 doubles it; a 4-ticks-a-year settle is an order of magnitude over the warm start. BL-764 is a representation change to the oldest layer in the generator and every pass downstream reads its output; it must split at promotion rather than be taken whole. (2) The 3-6 minute budget closes ONLY because the six candidates run in parallel. That makes determinism under threading the binding constraint - a winner chosen by completion order rather than by a deterministic argmax would be a non-deterministic world, which is the one invariant this project does not bend. retro.feedback:
THE SPRINT FOUND MORE THAN IT FIXED, and that is the result worth keeping. Two of the five new items are priority A and both are the same failure: a query tool returning a confident silent NO to "has this been built?". The session opened by answering that the archive union keeps that question answerable - the union is the right design and the hot/cold split is sound, but the union AS IMPLEMENTED sees 138 items of 762, and --grep throws away the landed matches it does find. An assumption stated in CLAUDE.md had never been measured.

The three boundary items came from the same mechanism at the doc grain: writing a one-line boundary is what exposes that the boundary was never stated. PRODUCTION and POPULATION each name the other as the workforce authority. TILE_GENERATION holds province rules the new headers point away from. Neither is visible while each doc is read alone.

Method note, and it is BL-791 demonstrated on the sprint that filed it: five slices read the whole ~650K corpus and the main session paid for none of it. The five reports came back as boundaries and findings, not excerpts.

BLOCK 2 IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE COLD REVIEW, MADE IN NUMBERS. Five lanes were built by capable agents working from settled instructions. FOUR FAILED. Not on style - on substance a self-report would never have surfaced: a lane deleted the ACCURATE half of a doubled claim and left the false half standing alone; a lane claimed to have grepped for dangling citations and had not; a lane asserted an answer in a doc after telling the judge the call was Ben's; a lane traded a false negative for a false positive and shipped doc text promising a behaviour its own code did not have. Every one was caught by an agent that had not written the change. Author-equals-reviewer would have merged all four.

AND THE SECOND REVIEW EARNED ITS KEEP TOO: it caught a fabricated "(Ben, 2026-09-07)" attribution on a rule that was mine, which would have hardened an agent's design call into a settled human ruling.

THE DESIGN PANEL CHANGED AN ANSWER. Two independent proposals per boundary - one arguing from CLAUDE.md's router, one licensed to say the router is wrong - split workforce differently from the way the filed item suggested. Had the builder just read the item, it would have built the wrong split confidently.

WHAT THE CRITIC PROVED ABOUT SCOPE. The three boundary lanes were scoped off defects a header sweep HAPPENED to notice. The critic built the Confused-with graph properly - 72 docs, 59 mutual pairs, 89 one-way edges - and found a confirmed duplicate, a triple-assertion and a one-way sprawl that no lane would have reached. BL-798 is the sharp lesson: BL-796 deleted copy two of the lens table on correct grounds and left copies three and four outside its write set, so the corpus is now MORE inconsistent on that subject, not less. A correct rule applied to a partial scope makes things worse. That is what BL-801 (header graph checker) exists to prevent, and it is why the tool comes before the next boundary sweep.

BLOCK 3 IS THE SPRINT'S OWN LESSON APPLIED TO ITSELF, AND THEN BROKEN AGAIN. BL-798 was filed because a lane applied a correct rule to a partial write set. The lane sent to FIX BL-798 did the same thing - consolidated copies two and three, left a verbatim fourth in a doc outside its write set, and reported a completeness search that was FALSE when the reviewer re-ran it. Widening the write set and demanding the search be pasted in full, empty results included, is what fixed it. The lesson is not "agents are careless": it is that a completeness claim is unverifiable from inside the scope that made it, so it must be re-run by someone else or it is not evidence.

THE TOOL WAS WORTH BUILDING FIRST AND ALSO NEEDED THE SAME TREATMENT. header_graph.js failed BOTH its cold reviews on the first cut. Its graph half stripped underscores along with markdown emphasis, so a third of the corpus could never be an edge target - and the specific defect it was built to catch, BL-799, was absent from its output. A checker that is merely plausible is worse than none, because it is trusted; the second reviewer's independent parser agreeing EDGE FOR EDGE is the only reason to believe the numbers now.

TWO AGENT ATTEMPTS FAILED THE SAME ITEM THE SAME WAY, and that is a signal to stop delegating. BL-799 was finished in the main session by reading the code site by site. Both agents wrote the tidy universal rule; the truth had an exception (corporation type words) that the corpus had ALREADY recorded elsewhere. When two independent attempts fail identically, the brief is wrong, not the agent.

AND THE SWEEP FOUND A CODE DEFECT THE DOCS WERE HIDING. BL-808: history_sim.cpp names a sim-founded region by appending the English word "Reach". The project fixed this exact defect once, in settlement.cpp, and wrote the post-mortem in a comment there - "two naming systems side by side in one string, which reads as a bug rather than a style". The second pass was never swept. A doc claim that was too broad is what exposed it: the tidy rule was wrong BECAUSE the code was wrong.
